summary: Robert von Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (~1851–1855) and served as Professor of Geography at the University of Giessen from 1864.

Robin Coningham specializes in archaeology and Indology. He earned his PhD at King's College, Cambridge (~1989–1994) under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held posts at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (from 2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~2005).

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School and Magdalen College (~1966–1969), completing doctoral research under John Hurrell Crook (~1969–1974). He held an academic post at University College London (~1987–1994).
Roderick Henry Macleod was an Indology scholar. He earned an M.A. at the University of Cambridge (~1913–1915), where he was appointed Lecturer in Indian Law in 1913.

Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown University and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1938–1942). He taught at the Barnes Foundation (~1946) and served as a professor at Brown University (~1947–1986), also holding posts at Graz and UMass Amherst.
Roderick S. Bucknell specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Queensland (~1976–2002), where he served as Associate Professor from ~1995 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with the British Museum (attested 1986), the University of London (attested 2010), and SOAS as Professor Emeritus (attested 2011, 2022).

Roger Billard worked in Indology. He studied at INALCO, EPHE, and under Louis Renou. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1945–1951) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1952–1979).

Roger Bischoff works in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin, and served as an Assistant Teacher at the International Meditation Centre (attested 1995).
Roger Brown was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his studies at the University of Michigan (~1946–1952) and held a post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Goossens specialized in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Université libre de Bruxelles (~1921–1926) studying under Émile Boisacq, Paul-Émile Dumont, and Henri Grégoire, later becoming Professor of Greek there in 1945.

Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris (until 1931). He held positions at the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle (~1929–1970), serving as its Director from ~1951 to 1965.
Roger Jeffery is a scholar in Indology and other fields. He earned his PhD at the University of Edinburgh (completed 1985), where he has held a post since 1972 as Professor (Emeritus).

Roger R. Jackson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1983) under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held posts at Fairfield University (attested 1986) and Carleton College (1990–2017).

Roger T. Ames works in philosophy and Sinology. He earned his PhD at SOAS under D. C. Lau (1975–1978). He spent his primary career at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1978–2016) and served as Fulbright Professor at Peking University (~2016).

Rohana Seneviratne works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. Educated at Peradeniya, Liverpool, and Oxford (DPhil 2015), he was a tutor at Liverpool and Oxford before serving as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Peradeniya (2022–2024).
Rohit Saluja works in computational fields and Indology. He holds posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Roland Barthes worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Émile Benveniste, later holding posts at CNRS (~1952–1959), EHESS (~1962–1977), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).

Roland Ferenczi works in Indology and history. He studied at the University of Pécs and Eötvös Loránd University. In 2024, he became an MSCA Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Hamburg and department head at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences Library.
